hero.headline: I am Matija Radeljak. I run Aning Film. This dashboard is one of the things I make.

why_this.title: Why this exists
paragraphs: I am a Croatian film producer. For 16 years I have been on the applying side of the table at HAVC — the Croatian Audiovisual Centre — and like every producer in this country I have spent a strange amount of my professional life inside their published PDFs, trying to remember who won what under which programme in which round.

HAVC publishes its decisions diligently and openly, but the trail lives across a thousand separate files. There is no single place to scan the whole 16-year arc, ask honest questions about it, and check the answers against the source. I built this so I — and any peer who has ever asked the same questions — would have one.

Everything you see is sourced from HAVC's own published documents. Where a number looks off, the dashboard lets you open the original PDF and check. The point is not to replace HAVC's record. The point is to make it navigable.

who_i_am.title: Who I am
paragraphs: I started on stage at seven and spent twelve years acting before I moved into film. I dropped out of an IT degree when it became obvious that filmmaking was the work, not the hobby. The IT part never quite left — every tool on this site is something I wrote.

I trained through the three European programmes that matter most for a producer of my generation: Maia Workshops, EAVE Producers Workshop, and TorinoFilmLab. I co-produced Breathing into Marble, which played East of the West at Karlovy Vary in 2018. The range of the rest of the work runs from a 200,000 EUR Allianz corporate event I produced and directed in 2010, to short films at Cannes Short Film Corner, to transmedia campaigns like Glowbrain and Croatia goes cross-media.

I wrote and run Dogma 23, a manifesto and a film gallery in Zagreb that argues cinema deserves to be exhibited with the care a painting gets. I built and maintain filmincroatia.com, the Filming in Croatia GPT, and a storyboard tool. Aning Film mentors filmmakers, runs workshops for children, and represents unrepresented European artists free of charge.

what_aning_is.title: What Aning Film is
paragraphs: Aning Film is a studio, not a company. It is a one-author practice that makes films, builds tools, runs platforms — and, occasionally, publishes a dataset like this one.

Everything signed Aning Film is signed by me. When the work is genuinely collaborative — a co-production, a director's project, a co-author — those collaborators are named directly. The royal we is not the house voice.
